name: Volume and surface area of solids
formula: V_{\text{prism, cyl}} = Bh, \quad V_{\text{pyramid, cone}} = \tfrac{1}{3}Bh, \quad V_{\text{sphere}} = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3, \quad S_{\text{sphere}} = 4\pi r^2, \quad S_{\text{cone side}} = \pi r \ell
whenToUse: Any problem about the volume of a solid, pouring liquid from one container into another, or the surface area of a sphere, cylinder or cone.
example: A cone with radius $3$ and height $4$ has slant height $5$, volume $\frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot 9 \cdot 4 = 12\pi$ and curved surface area $\pi \cdot 3 \cdot 5 = 15\pi$. A sphere of radius $3$ has volume $36\pi$.
pitfall: Pyramids and cones get the factor $\frac{1}{3}$; prisms and cylinders do not. The cone's side area uses the slant height $\ell$, not the vertical height.
